_readme: The Updates page and the 'Latest' cards on Home read this list. Add a new entry at the TOP. Fields: date (YYYY-MM-DD), tag (App, Robot, Brain, Face, Design, Website), title, text, and optional link + linkText. See docs/UPDATING.md.

updates.title: Android 1.0.4: meet the robot, join the waitlist
updates.text: The Android app now shows what Spike is becoming: a preview banner on Home, an Our story page with the robot renders, what he will do on your desk and how far the build has got, and a waitlist so you hear first when you can get one.

updates.title: Spike is on Android
updates.text: Spike 1.0.3 for Android is ready to download, for 64-bit phones. He opens straight into exploring: Face Studio, his face, pats and boops. To talk, remember, play and drive the robot he needs his brain, either a free Google Gemini key or a pairing code from Spike on a Windows PC. It is not on Google Play yet, so the page shows how to install it.

updates.title: Spike has a home on the web
updates.text: This site: what Spike is, the robot he is getting, the apps, and every update from here on.

updates.title: Body v3.2: the forehead tuft camera
updates.text: The camera moves to the centre of his forehead, hidden in a little tuft of fur. The chest gets a gesture window, the paws more desk clearance, and the rump two small ballast pockets so he stands steadier. 56 printed parts, about 382 g of print, and no clashes in the full assembly.

updates.title: One face
updates.text: The screen draws his eyes, nose and mouth, so the physical muzzle is gone. What says dog with the screen dark: the ears, the forehead tuft, the collar and the tag. Colour scheme: Caramel Pup.

updates.title: Spike for Windows 1.0.1
updates.text: Credits and polish: Settings now shows who made him and the exact version, and the Store listing and screenshots were refreshed.

updates.title: Spike 1.0 is on the Microsoft Store
updates.text: The first release passed Microsoft's certification. Talk or type to him, set alarms, design his face, and pair your phone and the robot. Free, with no account, no ads and no tracking.
updates.linkText: Get it on the Microsoft Store

updates.title: The phone app goes anywhere
updates.text: The Android app reaches Spike from any network with Tailscale, plays his voice from your computer, and runs a small brain of its own when he is away. It is in testing now.

updates.title: Firmware for both boards
updates.text: The screen board draws the face pixel for pixel like the reference, runs the body, the sensors and the gait, and keeps the desk-edge stops on at all times. Walking and give paw run in simulation and are waiting for the real body.

updates.title: The winking logo
updates.text: A cream screen face on a chocolate squircle, one eye winking and the tongue out. It is the app icon, the collar tag and the mark on this site.

updates.title: A brain that lives on your computer
updates.text: Conversation, personality, long-term memory, alarms and reminders, and a natural voice. What he remembers stays on your own computer, and you can make him forget anything.

updates.title: Face v2: Spike and Spicy
updates.text: A new animated face, drawn in code: moods, expressions, little games, and two characters, Spike the cheeky pup and Spicy the sassy cat.

updates.title: Body v3.1: fully covered
updates.text: Every servo, horn, screw and wire hidden inside a two-colour printed shell, like a finished product rather than a kit.

updates.title: The first bodies
updates.text: Versions 1 to 3 of the printed body, generated by scripts that drive SolidWorks, and the first interactive 3D preview of the shell.
